claim: research/evidence-dossier.md:26 "Ventura et al. 2020 meta-analysis: overall VR effect on empathy SDM = 0.43 (CI 0.31-0.55). https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1089/cyber.2019.0681" and research/evidence-dossier.md:28 "Another reported meta-analysis found perspective-taking d+ = 0.51 (wide CI 0.15-0.88) and a non-significant empathy effect (d+ = 0.21)."
evidence: WebSearch, search summaries only (a direct fetch of tmb.apaopen.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED). SDM = 0.43 [CI 0.31, 0.55], z = 6.93, is the overall effect in Martingano, Herrera & Konrath 2021, Technology, Mind, and Behavior (k = 43, N = 5,644): https://tmb.apaopen.org/pub/vr-improves-emotional-empathy-only ; https://scholarworks.indianapolis.iu.edu/items/7d7127c0-6c5e-4455-adea-d93c54ea48cc . Ventura et al. 2020 (Cyberpsychol Behav Soc Netw 23(10):667-676, 7 articles, 9 samples) reports in its journal abstract empathy d+ = 0.21 (CI -0.37 to 0.79, not significant) and perspective-taking d+ = 0.51 (CI 0.15 to 0.88): https://producciocientifica.uv.es/documentos/5fb86fc729995207311cbd94 . A repository preprint gives empathy d+ = 0.44 instead. So line 26 puts Martingano's pooled effect under Ventura's DOI. Line 28 is Ventura's own result, given with no author and no URL, which also fails the F03 criterion 'each finding has a URL'. The dossier therefore says Ventura found a significant moderate empathy effect, while Ventura's published abstract reports a non-significant one. A grep found these two figures only in the dossier. Fix: attribute 0.43 to Martingano 2021, and attribute the 0.51 / 0.21 figures to Ventura 2020 with its DOI. || VERIFIER 2026-10-09: Re-read research/evidence-dossier.md:25-28. Line 26 now gives Ventura et al. 2020 its own figures under its DOI (empathy d+ = 0.21, 95% CI -0.37 to 0.79, n.s.; perspective-taking d+ = 0.51, CI 0.15 to 0.88; 7 articles, 9 samples; earlier manuscript empathy d+ 0.44 noted). Line 27 attributes k = 43, N = 5,644, emotional d = 0.33 and cognitive d = 0.08 to Martingano, Herrera & Konrath 2021 with the tmb.apaopen.org and IU ScholarWorks URLs. Line 28 is now a synthesis of the two sourced lines. WebSearch (summary level; tmb.apaopen.org, scholarworks and intechopen are blocked by the proxy, curl 403 / ENOTFOUND) confirms the Ventura figures, the two-version empathy discrepancy (0.21 vs 0.44) and Martingano k = 43, N = 5,644, emotional d about 0.325. An extended search summary today did return the Martingano overall effect SDM = 0.43 [0.31, 0.55], z = 6.93 (attributed to the IU ScholarWorks PDF and the psycnet full text), so the auditor's attribution looks right; the owner's choice to keep it labelled unverified until the paper is read is conservative and acceptable, and the owner may now cite it as search-summary level. Grep: 0.43 / SDM appear nowhere else outside graph/audit. The misattribution is gone and line 28 no longer lacks a source. Fixed.
